item.title: Judge dismisses Trump administration lawsuit alleging antisemitism at Harvard University
item.description: The decision from U.S. District Judge Richard G. Stearns said that President Donald Trump's administration failed to prove an ongoing violation of federal civil rights laws.
item.content:encoded:
The decision from U.S. District Judge Richard G. Stearns said that President Donald Trump's administration failed to prove an ongoing violation of federal civil rights laws.

(Image credit: Steven Senne)

item.title: Judge drops Nevada case against electors accused of forging certificate in 2020 election
item.description: The dismissal marks the latest setback in swing states' efforts to prosecute fake electors who tried to keep Trump in the White House after he lost to Joe Biden in 2020.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: A summer canoe trip through New York's north woods to wild sand beaches
item.description: NPR's Brian Mann paddled the Ausable River in northern New York on a summer day to swim on wild sand beaches that stretch along Lake Champlain's shore.

item.title: Lawmakers and families raise concerns about conditions aboard U.S. aircraft carrier
item.description: Lawmakers and military families are raising concerns about conditions on board the USS Lincoln. The carrier, key to the administration's war with Iran, has been at sea for over 250 days.

item.title: Kennedy Center Board votes again to shut main building down — and add Trump's name back
item.description: The board voted to close the Washington, D.C., arts complex's main campus for a $250 million renovation — three months after a federal judge temporarily blocked a similar closure.
